text: An AnimationManager is not driven by any scene, even when created with the scene's engine: its groups and tasks wait for updateAnimationManager. onBeforeRender(scene, (d) => updateAnimationManager(manager, d)) runs it every frame.

AnimationGroup.currentTime and duration are seconds, not frames. Each update moves currentTime by deltaMs / 1000 * speedRatio, and goToFrame turns its frame into seconds by dividing by frameRate, which is 60 when none was given.

createPropertyAnimationGroup attaches the group to the manager and starts it playing, with loopAnimation true unless loop: false is passed. It writes nothing to the target until the next updateAnimationManager.

Each updateAnimationManager first advances currentTime, then writes the value at the new time, so a first update of 16 ms writes the value at 0.016 s. updateAnimationManager(manager, 0) writes the value at the current time.

A non-looping property group clamps at the range end, writes the last value and sets isPlaying to false in that same update. Later updates do not write the target, and the group stays in getAnimationGroups.
A looping property group wraps currentTime modulo its range, so exactly at the range end it writes the first key's value, not the last. 2500 ms into a 1 s loop, currentTime is 0.5.
Key values and key times are stored in a Float32Array, so written values are float32-rounded: a key value of 0.1 is written as 0.10000000149011612, and an exact === 0.1 check fails.

@babylonjs/lite does not export evaluateSampler, evaluatePropertySampler, tickAnimationCore, tickAnimation, getAnimationGroupOwner, ANIMATION_GROUP_TASK_CATEGORY, INTERP_*, PATH_* or any _ function. group._animationManager is the owner.

Every part of a track's dotted path must exist on the target when createPropertyAnimationGroup runs, or it throws. For a multi-value key, the property's set(...) is called if it has one; otherwise its x, y, z, w fields are written.

A key's time is seconds; its frame is divided by the track's frameRate, else the clip's, which is options.frameRate, else tracks[0].frameRate, else 60. A key with both or neither of time and frame throws.

A property group's weight has no effect unless enablePropertyAnimationBlending was called on the manager. Without it each group writes its full value, and on a shared property the later-attached group wins.

Under enablePropertyAnimationBlending, a property is mixed when a group on it has weight other than 1. The mix is the plain sum of value * weight, not divided by the total weight: one group at 0.5 writes half its value.

fadeAnimationWeight only tweens group.weight, linearly, by each update's step and before the groups are evaluated; it turns on no blending. from is applied at once, and a new fade on the same group replaces the old one.
crossFadeAnimationGroups only changes the two weights: it does not play toGroup or stop fromGroup, which keeps playing at weight 0. A durationMs of 0 throws, in fadeAnimationWeight too.
pauseAnimation stops both advancing and writing. stopAnimation also sets currentTime to the range start but writes nothing, so the target keeps its last animated value.
goToFrame pauses the group. On a property group it writes the value at once, with the time clamped to 0..clip duration rather than to the play range, and playAnimation then resumes from that time.

playAnimation on a finished property group leaves currentTime at the end, so the next update ends it again. stopAnimation then playAnimation replays from the start; a seek before playAnimation replays from the seek.

Every easing function but bezierCurveEase is an ease-in curve, and there is no easing mode; (g) => 1 - cubicEase(1 - g) gives ease-out. A track's easing reshapes each span between two keys, not the whole clip.

runFrameInterpolation calls step once per scene frame with the delta in seconds (16 ms gives 0.016); a delta of 0 or less becomes 1/60. The first call comes on the next frame, not during runFrameInterpolation.

Once step returns false it is never called again, and the promise resolves on a later microtask, not inside the frame. If step throws, the promise rejects with an Error; a thrown string becomes its message.
Clip duration is the latest key time over all tracks, and a group plays from 0 to duration by default. Before a track's first key it holds the first value; after its last key, the last value.
fromFrame and toFrame are divided by the clip frameRate. The group starts at fromTime, loops within fromTime..toTime, and stopAnimation puts currentTime back to fromTime.
A 4-value track slerps only when quaternion: true is set or its path is, or ends with, rotationQuaternion. Otherwise each component is lerped on its own and the result is not normalized.
A track with interpolation "step" holds each key's value until the next key's time, and switches exactly at that time.

enableAnimationBlending and enablePropertyAnimationBlending fill the same single slot on a manager, so the last call wins. setAnimationAdditive on a group already in a manager calls enableAnimationBlending, turning property blending off.
Under enablePropertyAnimationBlending, a property whose groups all have weight 0 is not written. Two groups both at weight 1 are not mixed: the later-attached one wins.
createPropertyAnimationGroup throws unless toTime > fromTime, so a clip whose keys all sit at time 0 (duration 0) throws unless toTime is passed.

A multi-value track on a property with no set() and no x field, like {r, g, b} or an array, throws at createPropertyAnimationGroup, as does a key of more than 4 values. A number key replaces the property itself.
Assigning group.currentTime is a seek: the next update advances from it and writes. Setting isPlaying = true on a finished group does nothing, even after a seek.
With fixedDeltaMs above 0, every updateAnimationManager uses it and ignores the deltaMs passed, even 0, negative or NaN. Without it, a negative or non-finite deltaMs makes the update do nothing.
Tasks run in the order added, and each attached group is one of those tasks. A task added during an update first runs on the next update; one removed during an update before its turn does not run.

removeAnimationGroup stops the manager advancing the group but leaves isPlaying true and the target as it was. addAnimationGroup puts a removed group back at its first-attachment place in the order, not last.
addAnimationGroup throws for a group owned by another manager and does nothing for its own. getAnimationGroups returns the manager's live array, and clearAnimationManager detaches every group.
With an already aborted signal, runFrameInterpolation rejects at once with signal.reason wrapped as an Error, and step never runs. Aborting later detaches the step and rejects.
createAnimationGroups makes only the first group playing; the rest stay stopped until playAnimation. An unnamed clip's group is named animation_<index>, and frameRate is 60 when the clip has none.
A glTF group with loopAnimation false clamps currentTime at the clip end but keeps isPlaying true; only property groups set isPlaying to false at their end.
glTF groups added to a scene by addToScene advance with the scene each frame until addAnimationGroup hands them to a manager. After removeAnimationGroup, the scene advances them again.
A glTF group does not pick up a change to mask.names made in place at the same length, like names[0] = "arm". It does pick up a new names array, a push, or a change to mode or disabled.
A mask matches glTF node names exactly, case included, and Include is the default mode. A masked-out node that has a scene target is set to its rest pose on every tick.
Easing output is not clamped, so backEase and elasticEase go past the keys' values. Easing is skipped on step tracks, before the first key and from the last key on.
A negative speedRatio plays backward. A looping group wraps; a non-looping one stops moving at fromTime but keeps isPlaying true.

A property group's targetedAnimations has { target, path } per track: the object owning the last path part, and that part, so "position.x" gives position and "x". duration is the whole clip's, even with a narrower range.
startAnimationManager throws where requestAnimationFrame is missing, as in Node. In its loop the first frame's delta is 0, and onUpdate is called only by that loop, never by updateAnimationManager.
removeAnimationTask and clearAnimationManager set active to false and call dispose. A task with active false is skipped, and addAnimationTask to its own manager does not set active back to true.
setAnimationWeight throws for a weight outside 0..1 or not finite. Assigning group.weight directly is not checked.
goToFrame on a looping glTF group wraps the time: frame 90 of a 1 s clip at 60 fps gives 0.5 s. On a stopped glTF group it sets currentTime but applies the pose only when engine is passed.
Under enableAnimationBlending, a glTF group with weight other than 1 makes updateAnimationManager throw unless the manager was created with engine. Such a group does not write its scene node targets.
Under enablePropertyAnimationBlending, a paused group with weight other than 1 still writes its weighted value at its currentTime each update. A stopped group writes nothing.
The path is resolved again at each write: if target.position is replaced, later writes go to the new object. If a path part is deleted, updateAnimationManager throws.
A glTF group's targetedAnimations has one entry per channel, with nodeIndex, targetName from nodeNames, target from nodeTargets, and path "translation", "rotation", "scale", "weights" or "pointer".
